The king is mortal, and the shepherd is mortal. The gods are immortal. Honor the Allotter, and he will give a long thread.

english: The Twin and his brother were alone. There was no sea, and there was no sky. Then the brother slew him with a knife. From his flesh he created the earth, and from his bones the stones. From his blood he created the water, and from his eyes the sun. From his head he created the sky, and from his breath the wind. From his mind he created the moon, and from his mouth the fire. The earth is the body of the Twin. When a mortal dies, his bones go to the stones, and his breath flies to the wind.

english: Yonder flows a black river. No man swims through it, and no fish lives in it. An old man waits at the ford with a boat. He carries the dead over the water. He takes a wage from the dead: bronze. He questions each dead man: "Whose son are you?" The dead man says the name of his parent. Then he carries him in the boat. Whoever does not know his own lineage stays here in the cold, crying. So a man teaches his boy his lineage.

english: Old Bright-Mind was lying on his bed, and he called his three sons. "I am going to the forebears. Divide the herd, and take your own portion. Do not fight, brothers. In spring pour milk for me beside the stone. Set the names of the forebears on your offspring. Lay me on the hill, under the oak. So our line will not vanish." Then he fell asleep, and his breath went to the wind. The brothers lifted his body onto the wagon.

english: I am Good-Horses, daughter of Kindly, granddaughter of Divine-Race. My mother was Well-Born, the granddaughter of a king. My grandmother wove this garment from wool. The hands of the grandmother were swift. Its threads are red and white. Well-Born wore it, and now I wear it. When I am dead, my daughter will wear it, and my granddaughter after her. In this garment live the hands of our mothers.

pie: h₁suḱléwēs h₁ésyo ǵn̥h₁tréy h₁suménesey ḱóm h₂éḱmonm̥ stoh₂éyet. h₁suménēs kóryoy h₁ésyo déms h₂epó séngʷt. só h₂nr̥ḱléwesos suHnús h₁suh₁éḱwosyo-kʷe népōts h₁ést. h₁ésyo bʰréh₂teres pótnih₂-kʷe HrudHént. deywṓs tósmey h₁uséwōm dh₃ih₁ént. ḱós h₂éḱmō sth₂éh₁yēti h₁ésyo-kʷe h₁nómn̥ ne néḱeti. h₁yós tóm dʰégʷʰh₂eti h₁suménesm̥ memn̥yéh₁t. lewkómenēs wékʷesh₂ péyḱt.
english: Good-Fame set up this stone for his parent, Kindly. Kindly fell in war, away from his home. He was the son of Man-Fame and the grandson of Good-Horses. His brothers and his wife cried. May the gods give him good things. This stone will stand, and his name will not vanish. Whoever passes by it, may he remember Kindly. Bright-Mind carved the words.

pie: h₁suménēs h₂yuHn̥ḱṓy h₂nr̥ḱléwesey wérh₁t. súHnew dwóh₁ stóygʰoh₁ tébʰye h₂énti sth₂éh₁yetes. h₁yód démi ménēsi dl̥h₁gʰóm h₂óyu gʷíh₃wēsi h₁nómn̥-kʷe toy néḱeti. h₁yód kóryom gʷéh₂esi moḱs séngʷesi ń̥dʰgʷʰitom-kʷe toy ḱléwos h₁éseti. wl̥h₁dʰí. h₂nr̥ḱléwēs ḱléwos wélh₁t. HeHḱúns h₁éḱwons yéwgt kʷékʷlom-kʷe kóryom h₂éǵet. polh₁úns póyḱons gʷʰént pr̥wéni-kʷe moḱs séngʷt. h₁suménēs HréwdHt. h₁ésyeh₂s dáḱruh₂ h₂éyeri gʰr̥h₁méni h₁épi légʰeti. nu h₂néres h₁ím gʷr̥nHénti. wiHrósyo ḱléwos ne mért.
english: Kindly spoke to the young Man-Fame: "Son, two paths stand before you. If you stay at home, you will live a long life, and your name will vanish. If you go to war, you will fall early, and imperishable fame will be yours. Choose!" Man-Fame chose fame. He yoked the swift horses and drove the chariot to war. He slew many enemies, and he fell early at the ford. Kindly cried. In the morning her tears lie on the grass. Now men praise him. The fame of a hero does not die.

pie: ǵérh₂onts mógʰum prḗḱst kʷóti ǵénh₁torn̥s wóydth₂e? septḿ̥ ǵénh₁torn̥s wóydh₂e. lewkómenēs h₁suménēs pr̥h₂wóḱlewēs h₁suǵénh₁ēs ḱlutóǵenh₁ēs deywóh₁eḱwos h₁sustóygʰos-kʷe. septm̥mós deywósyo suHnús h₁ést. h₂éǵt h₁yós septḿ̥ ǵénh₁torn̥s wóyde só h₁léwdʰeros. túH h₁léwdʰeros. méwdt mogʰéwey-kʷe h₂éyesos ḱéstrom déh₃t.
english: The old man asked the boy: "How many forebears do you know?" "I know seven forebears: Bright-Mind, Kindly, First-Fame, Well-Born, Of-Famous-Race, Divine-Horses and Good-Path. The seventh was the son of a god." He said: "Whoever knows seven forebears, he is free. You are free." He rejoiced and gave the boy a knife of bronze.

pie: suHnús h₁suwékʷesey ne ǵn̥h₁yéto h₁ésyo téḱnom dʰugh₂tḗr h₁ést. h₁suwékʷēs h₂éǵt kʷís moy wódr̥ ǵʰéwete h₁yód h₁eǵóh₂ mr̥tós h₁ésoh₂? HeHḱuménesey h₁ésyo dʰugh₂térm̥ déh₃t h₂éǵt-kʷe tósyeh₂s moy mógʰus suHnús h₁éseti. mógʰus tósyeh₂ey ǵn̥h₁yéto h₁suwékʷēs h₁ím tl̥néh₂t h₁ésmey-kʷe h₁nómn̥ dʰéh₁t. túH moy suHnús népōts-kʷe. nu h₁suwékʷesos ǵenh₁eséh₂ ne néḱt.
english: No son was born to Good-Word; his child was a daughter. Good-Word said: "Who will pour water for me when I am dead?" He gave his daughter to Swift-Mind and said: "Her boy will be my son." A boy was born to her; Good-Word lifted him and set a name on him. "You are my son and my grandson." So the line of Good-Word did not vanish.

pie: pótey moḱs séngʷs h₁mé-kʷe h₁widʰéwh₂m̥ démi léykʷs. suHnús nos h₂yuHn̥ḱós. kʷís tóm h₂léksēti? kʷís h₁mé h₂léksēti? póyḱōs gʷémonti n̥smé-kʷe h₂epó wédʰōnti. téwe moy ǵʰóstom ne déh₃s wékʷos moy ne wérh₁s. h₁éḱwōs toy dʰwóri h₂énti sth₂éh₁yonti twé-kʷe ménonti. stérh₃mn̥ toy ḱolHtóm. nu HréwdHmi gʷénh₂es-kʷe méǵʰye ḱóm HrudHénti. ḱléwos toy méǵh₂ ḱéh₂dos-kʷe moy méǵh₂.
english: Husband, you fell early and left me a widow in the house. Our son is young. Who will protect him? Who will protect me? Enemies will come and lead us away. You did not give me your hand; you did not speak a word to me. Your horses stand by the door and wait for you. Your bed is cold. Now I cry, and the women cry with me. Your fame is great, and my grief is great.

pie: wiHrósyo h₁éḱwoh₁ n̥mr̥tóh₁ h₁stā́m h₂énh₁mōd ǵn̥h₁yónto. tóysōm méh₂tēr gʰréh₁mn̥ déh₂newi h₂énti h₁ḗdt h₂énh₁mos tā́m gʷémt. dwóh₁ HeHḱúh₁ h₁éḱwoh₁ ǵénh₁t. deywṓs h₁ésmey tóh₁ dh₃ént. h₁yód wiHrós séngʷt h₁éḱwoh₁ HrudHtā́m. tóysōm dáḱruh₂ dʰéǵʰōm sréwet. ne h₁édtām ne-kʷe píph₃etām. dyḗws tóh₁ dérḱt h₂éǵt-kʷe. kʷíd mórtōy usmé dh₃mé? yúH n̥mr̥tṓs só mr̥tós h₁ést.
english: The hero's horses were immortal; they were born of the wind. Their mother was eating grass beside a river; the wind came to her. She bore two swift horses. The gods gave them to him. When the hero fell, the horses cried. Their tears flowed to the earth. They did not eat, and they did not drink. Sky looked at them and said: "Why did we give you to a mortal? You are immortal; he was mortal."

pie: dwóh₁ wiHróh₁ kóryoysu h₁entér h₁ludʰétām. sénos prḗḱst kʷís toy ph₂tḗr? h₂yuHn̥ḱós wérh₁t ph₂tḗr moy ḱlutóǵenh₁ēs. só h₂epó gʷéh₂t h₁mé-kʷe téḱnom ḱóymoy léykʷt. só mr̥twós ne néseti. ǵérh₂onts h₁ím ǵn̥néh₃t h₂éǵt-kʷe h₁eǵóh₂ toy ph₂tḗr. h₂yuHn̥ḱós wérh₁t ǵérh₂ont me dʰrugʰyési. nu ǵʰoysóns Hih₁ktā́m. wikétām ḱlutóǵenh₁esos-kʷe ǵʰoysós h₂yuHn̥ḱóm kélh₂t. ḱlutóǵenh₁ēs HréwdHt swóm suHnúm gʷʰénm̥. nu ḱlutóǵenh₁esos ǵenh₁eséh₂ néḱt.
english: Two heroes came between the troops. The elder asked: "Who is your father?" The young one spoke: "My father is Of-Famous-Race. He went away and left me in the household as a child. He is dead; he will not return." The old man recognized him and said: "I am your father." The young one spoke: "You deceive me, old man." Then they threw spears. They fought, and the spear of Of-Famous-Race struck the young one. Of-Famous-Race cried: "I have slain my own son." So the line of Of-Famous-Race vanished.
